lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Present for 60–90 seconds with Q&A. Note one question and whether you used evidence or said you need to check. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Original response on new material: Question → findings → visual/source → invite questions. Reasoning: I used present by attending to research rather than copying the worked model.

Parent: Written model 2: Common error: Inventing an answer in Q&A breaks research honesty. Correction: Question → findings → visual/source → invite questions. Why: the correction restores accurate use of present.

Parent: Likely misconception: Inventing an answer in Q&A breaks research honesty. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Produce a fresh example demonstrating present on new material (not the worked model). Explain the particular words, sources or choices that make it work.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one likely error with present, correct it, and explain why the correction helps a reader or audience.

WORKED MODEL

teach_steps.explain:
Presenting the research project means stating the question, key findings and sources, then answering questions without inventing data.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make decisions based on specific language evidence, rather than guess or copy someone else. Keep the meaning accurate and explain the choice.

HOW TO WORK
Read the original example and locate the words or actions that support the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Check your response against the feedback: did you address the same skill and show your reasoning? If a detail is uncertain, identify what would have to be checked. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than making the answer longer.
